name: INA241A3IDDFR
title: INA241A, INA241B: –5 V to 110 V bidirectional precision current-sense amplifiers with enhanced PWM rejection, gains 10 to 200 V/V
summary: Single-channel, zero-drift current-sense amplifiers that read a shunt at any common-mode voltage from –5 V to 110 V on a 2.7 V to 20 V supply, with circuitry that suppresses the output disturbance from fast PWM common-mode edges up to 125 kHz. Version A holds offset to ±10 µV and gain error to ±0.01 %, version B to ±150 µV and ±0.1 %; each comes in gains of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 V/V with 1.1 MHz bandwidth. Two reference pins set the zero-current output for unidirectional or bidirectional sensing. INA241A3IDDFR is version A, gain 50 V/V, in an 8-pin SOT-23-THIN.
key_figures: –5 V to 110 V operating; –20 V to 120 V survival

circuits.title: Inline motor current sensing
circuits.description: A bridge of six IGBTs on a 48 V bus drives a 48 V, 4000 RPM motor through three leads; a 100 mΩ shunt sits in one lead and an INA241A2 (gain 20) on a 5 V supply reads it while that lead swings with the PWM. REF1 on 5 V and REF2 on ground put the zero-current output at mid-supply, so current in either direction is measured.

circuits.title: Ground-referenced unidirectional output
circuits.description: Both reference pins on ground: the output rests at ground with no sense voltage and rises as IN+ goes positive relative to IN-.

circuits.title: VS-referenced unidirectional output
circuits.description: Both reference pins on VS: the output rests at the supply with no sense voltage and falls toward ground as IN+ goes negative relative to IN-. It lets the amplifier output and the control circuitry settle before the load is powered.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.

circuits.title: Output set to an external reference
circuits.description: REF1 and REF2 tied together to a REF5025 2.5 V reference: the output sits at 2.5 V with no sense voltage and moves above or below it with the sign of the sense voltage. Of the reference schemes, this one places the zero-current output most precisely.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.

circuits.title: Output set to mid-supply
circuits.description: REF1 on VS and REF2 on ground: the output sits at VS / 2 with no sense voltage, an offset that tracks the supply, and swings either way for bidirectional current.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.

circuits.title: Output set to half an external reference
circuits.description: REF1 on a REF5025 2.5 V reference and REF2 on ground: the internal divider halves the reference, so the output sits at 1.25 V with no sense voltage.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.

circuits.title: Reference set by a resistor divider
circuits.description: R1 and R2 divide VS and drive both reference pins. OUT goes to the ADC as a differential signal against the divider node; read single-ended against ground, the shift in internal impedance degrades the specified performance.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.

circuits.title: Reference set by a buffered resistor divider
circuits.description: R1 and R2 divide VS; an op amp wired as a follower buffers the divider node and drives both reference pins, so OUT can be read single-ended by an ADC.
notes: NC is reserved and goes to ground per its pin function.
The op amp's supply pins are not shown.

circuits.title: Test circuit for reference divider accuracy

operation.text: A zero-drift, bidirectional current-sense amplifier for high-side, low-side or inline (motor phase) shunts. Fixed gains of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 V/V let the full-scale output be matched to the current range. A PWM-rejection stage at the inputs keeps fast common-mode edges from showing at the output.

INA241A and INA241B share pinout, gains and packages and differ in accuracy: version A has ±10 µV maximum offset (±0.1 µV/°C drift) and ±0.01 % maximum gain error (±1 ppm/°C), version B ±150 µV (±0.5 µV/°C) and ±0.1 % (±5 ppm/°C). The suffix digit 1 to 5 picks the gain. INA241A3IDDFR is version A, gain 50 V/V, in the 8-pin SOT-23-THIN (DDF), 3000 per reel.

The inputs work from –5 V to 110 V of common mode and survive –20 V to 120 V, whatever the 2.7 V to 20 V supply is; with VS at 5 V the shunt may sit at 110 V. The output, however, stays inside the supply: from about 20 mV above ground to 200 mV below VS.

When the device detects a large common-mode dV/dt edge it holds the output for 1 µs so the disturbance does not reach it. A further edge within the next 3 µs is handled by the amplifier's bandwidth and AC CMRR alone. The full benefit applies up to 125 kHz PWM, or whenever edges are at least 3 µs apart. AC CMRR is 104 dB at 100 kHz and 89 dB at 1 MHz.

Small-signal bandwidth is 1.1 MHz at every gain, slew rate 8 V/µs, and a step settles to 1 % in 1 µs. On a 2 mΩ shunt at gain 20, a 75 A over-current threshold gives 3 V at the output, reached in under 1 µs.

Each input draws about 35 µA, and this stays constant over the whole common-mode range up to 110 V instead of rising with common-mode voltage. With the supply off (VS = 0 V) the input current is near zero.

Gain error is ±0.01 % maximum at room temperature with ±1 ppm/°C drift (version A, gains 10 to 50). The gain is chosen for signal-to-noise ratio, dynamic current range and the full-scale output voltage wanted.

REF1 and REF2 feed matched precision resistors in the gain network and are interchangeable. With zero sense voltage the output sits at the mean of the two reference voltages. Both on ground or both on VS gives unidirectional operation (sense voltage must then be positive or negative respectively). One on VS and one on GND gives VS / 2; both on an external reference gives that voltage; one on a reference and one on ground gives half of it. The pins are meant to be driven from VS, GND or a stiff (low source impedance) reference; a resistor divider on them needs a buffer if the output is read single-ended.

Shunt value, current range, gain option and reference voltage together have to keep the output between its swing limits to ground and to VS. A larger shunt raises the signal and lowers the share of offset error, limited by its dissipation; a higher gain allows a smaller shunt and less dissipation.
Decouple VS with 0.1 µF placed as close to the VS and GND pins as possible; add more capacitance when the supply is noisy or has high source impedance.

Run IN+ and IN– to the shunt as a Kelvin (4-wire) connection so that only the shunt's own resistance lies between them; any extra current-carrying copper in that path is a significant error against a milliohm shunt. In the recommended layout the shunt sits beside pins 1 and 8, the bypass capacitor next to VS (pin 6), and GND, REF2 and NC go by vias to the ground plane, REF1 by a via to ground, VS by a via to the supply.
Automotive AEC-Q100 versions are separate devices, INA241A-Q1 and INA241B-Q1.
